question.text: A particle executes simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and time period is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The time it will take to travel from its position of maximum displacement to the point corresponding to half of its amplitude, is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>

solution.text:
Given here, A=8 cm and T=6 s

The displacement equation in SHM, when amplitude is halved is Acos2πtT=A2

⇒2πtT=π3

Time taken by the particle is t= T6=66=1sec.
